title: Choose the Peterson homepage world
question: Choose the world that should shape the homepage brief, or re-roll for a fresh hand. Every option preserves the supplied Peterson lockup in burgundy or white, treats burgundy as the fixed brand color, and keeps the residential-first message and confirmed conversion hierarchy.

options.label: Beneath the Grade
options.lineage: geotechnical boring logs and site-section records
options.thesis: The homepage reveals a finished homesite as the visible result of disciplined work below the surface.
options.viewport: The Peterson logo and estimate action sit above a full-width grade line: project video owns the land above it while a precise cutaway below names the complete sequence from clearing through finish preparation; the headline sits directly on the grade.
options.risk: Without plain-language labels and warm residential proof, the technical discipline could feel like an engineering consultancy.

raised.raise: Every service stage now resolves against one shared site-readiness scale rather than a loose collection of cards.
Large, unmistakable wayfinding landmarks keep the technical world scannable for homeowners.
The signature grade-line interaction demonstrates cause and effect instead of decorating the page.

options.label: The Stake Book
options.lineage: surveyor field books, staking plans, and fluorescent site flags
options.thesis: A homeowner sees the whole job organized as a confident field plan before the first bucket moves.
options.viewport: An asymmetrical field-book spread places the supplied logo in the binding margin, the headline and estimate action on a clean planning sheet, and an authentic project-video frame under numbered stake annotations that lead into the six service groups.
options.risk: Construction-document language is familiar and effective, so timid execution could slip into a conventional blueprint theme.

options.label: The Sitework Field Guide
options.lineage: hand-drawn technical zines and annotated jobsite sketches
options.thesis: Complete site work becomes a plainspoken, step-by-step guide a homeowner can understand at a glance.
options.viewport: The real Peterson logo anchors a bright field-guide sheet; the headline, estimate button, and authentic video slot sit beside one annotated diagram tracing clearing, excavation, utilities, septic, driveway, and finish preparation.
options.case: It matches the homeowner’s need for clarity, but its playful hand can undercut the seriousness and durability expected of excavation work.
options.risk: Too much doodle language would make an experienced contractor feel casual or juvenile.

options.label: One Job at a Time
options.thesis: Authentic work is the interface: each project fills the screen and proves one stage of complete site preparation.
options.viewport: A verified project video fills the page behind the Peterson logo and fixed estimate action; a restrained stage rail moves from raw parcel to ready homesite while call and text remain immediate on mobile.
options.case: It gives authentic proof exceptional force, but one immersive project at a time makes service breadth slower to understand.
options.risk: The feed grammar may feel fashionable and media-led rather than established and service-led.

options.label: Below the Surface
options.lineage: technical depth profiles and expedition logs
options.thesis: The page descends through the hidden layers of a residential site, then returns to the finished grade with proof in hand.
options.viewport: A vertical depth rail crosses a wide authentic excavation frame; the headline and estimate action occupy the surface zone while utility, septic, foundation, drainage, and aggregate layers descend beneath it.
options.case: The depth structure explains excavation beautifully, but its expedition lineage identifies less naturally with a residential customer than a real field record.
options.risk: A dark technical atmosphere can feel remote unless balanced with daylight, homesites, and human-scale copy.

options.label: Site Readiness Bridge
options.thesis: Six synchronized gauges show a property moving toward ready-to-build status.
options.viewport: A row of service-stage gauges sits beneath the headline and project frame.
options.case: The synchronization is useful, but homeowners do not naturally identify excavation through audio instrumentation.
options.kept: One shared readiness scale now unifies the assigned direction’s service stages.
options.risk: The metaphor must be explained before it helps.

options.label: Jobsite Sign River
options.lineage: night-market sign rivers translated into site markers
options.thesis: Survey flags and temporary signs lead visitors through service zones like landmarks across a working site.
options.viewport: A route of jobsite markers crosses the project video toward the estimate action.
options.case: The navigation is memorable, but the market lineage distracts from residential trust and complete-site-work clarity.
options.kept: Large visual landmarks now make the assigned technical world easy to scan.
options.risk: Color and signs can become noisy before they become useful.

options.label: Grade-Flow Garden
options.lineage: interactive gravity-field gardens translated into drainage and grade
options.thesis: Moving the grade line makes water, access, and site preparation visibly respond.
options.viewport: A responsive terrain field surrounds the project message and estimate action.
options.case: Cause and effect is compelling, but the surreal world weakens product clarity and could imply design services Peterson does not offer.
options.kept: The assigned grade-line interaction must explain site consequence, not act as decoration.
options.risk: A simulation can overpromise technical design capability.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished excavation-company homepage built around a dark project-video hero, service cards, credentials, reviews, and a strong estimate button.
canonCard.viewport: The supplied Peterson logo sits over a full-width project-video hero with Local Experience. Solid Results., Request an Estimate, Call, and Text; service cards begin below the fold.
canonCard.risk: It is easy to understand but intentionally resembles the best version of the category rather than owning a distinctive Peterson mechanism.
